newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed, trail Wall St. gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed, trail Wall St. gains.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished mixed on Tuesday after a light session as investors slowly returned from the summer's last holiday weekend.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 8.46 points to close at 5151.89 in moderate volume of 56.1 million shares valued at C$708.6 million (US$516 million).
The market ended with declining stocks outnumbering advancers 428 to 412 and 284 issues closing flat.
"After returning from a long holiday, obviously some people haven't decided what to do yet," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Toronto opened lower with New York amid investor jitters over U.S. air strikes on Iraq and a possible rise in U.S. interest rates.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rebounded later in the day to finish with a 32-point gain.
Ketchen said oil stocks received a boost from the Iraqi situation, which sparked a surge in oil prices earlier today. Gold issues also benefited from an early rally in bullion.
Interest rate sensitive stocks were depressed by concerns that the U.S. Federal Reserve may hike rates later this month.
* Barrick Gold Corp. topped the most-active list, up 0.60 at 37.55 on 1.6 million shares. Other shining gold stocks included Placer Dome Inc, up 0.30 at 33.30.
Getchell Gold Corp. led net gainers, soaring 4.85 to 61.60 in light volume.

* Among energy stocks, Renaissance Energy Ltd. rose 0.80 to 39.30, while Imperial Oil jumped 0.85 to 59.95. Crude prices climbed on news that the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food plan is on hold following a U.S. missile strike on Iraq.
* Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc. sank 3.25 to 100.25 as investors reacted to the company's plan to acquire U.S.-based Arcadian Corp. in a cash and stock deal.
